title: Sales agent: semantic model for Dynamics 365 and Salesforce CRM data
summary: The briefing's controls, licensing and rollout statements are supported, including the glossary API and the navigation steps flagged by the pre-check. Two minor qualifications would make conflicting Microsoft documentation about defaults and lifecycle management clearer.

claims.claim: The roadmap lists the feature as In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap targets general availability for December CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "December CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview target is October CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "October CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The listed platforms are Desktop, Mobile, Teams and Surface Devices, and Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Desktop", "Mobile", "Teams and Surface Devices", "Web"]

claims.claim: This roadmap item concerns Sales agent in Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365).
claims.quote: "title": "Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): Enable semantic model in Sales agent"

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified on November 11, 2026.
Microsoft plans a connected representation of CRM structure and meaning that Sales agent can retrieve when answering.
claims.quote: Semantic model helps Sales Agent understand the structure and meaning of an organization’s CRM data.

claims.claim: The roadmap's model covers tables or objects, fields, descriptions, data types, relationships, views, pick-list values and glossary terms.
claims.quote: including tables or objects, fields, descriptions, data types, relationships, views, pick-list values, and glossary terms

claims.claim: The roadmap says the model should help answer complex questions spanning related CRM records.
claims.quote: improving its ability to interpret business language and answer complex questions that span related CRM records

claims.claim: The roadmap says Dynamics 365 admins can turn on the semantic model in Power Apps Maker Portal.
claims.quote: Dynamics 365 admins can enable and turn on semantic model in Power Apps Maker Portal

claims.claim: Dynamics 365 admins can configure the underlying data coverage, views, metadata and relationships.
claims.quote: Admins can configure the underlying data, views, metadata and relationships used in the model.

claims.claim: For Salesforce, the roadmap says the model starts from existing Sales agent table and glossary configuration.
claims.quote: For Salesforce customers, the semantic model will be based on existing Sales agent table and glossary configuration in Sales agent settings or Power Apps Maker Portal.

claims.claim: Salesforce admins can configure additional relationships and views in the maker portal under the roadmap plan.
claims.quote: In Power Apps Maker Portal, Salesforce admins will can configure additional Salesforce signals to use in semantic model such as relationships and views.

claims.claim: Microsoft published MC1540293 on November 5, 2026.
claims.quote: Published 2026-11-05; last updated 2026-11-05

claims.claim: MC1540293 gives November 17, 2026 as general availability, differing from the roadmap target.
claims.quote: This feature will reach general availability on November 17, 2026.

claims.claim: MC1540293 is for awareness and requires no administrator action.
claims.quote: This message is for awareness, and no action is required.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; controls notes; Risk assessment
claims.claim: The Sales agent semantic-model setup section is still marked preview.
claims.quote: Step 2: Configure the semantic model (preview)

claims.claim: Learn directs admins to enable Work IQ and then fine-tune the generated model.
claims.quote: Follow the steps to turn on Work IQ in your environment. ... To refine how Sales agent interprets your data, review and adjust the signals in the generated model.

claims.claim: On Dynamics 365, the semantic model is generated automatically after enabling the setting.
claims.quote: Dynamics 365: The model is automatically generated after you enable the setting.

claims.claim: On Salesforce, generation occurs at the next metadata cache refresh.
claims.quote: Salesforce: The model isn't generated immediately after you enable the setting. It's generated on the next metadata cache refresh.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The model extracts context from relationships, views, forms and table or column descriptions.
claims.quote: The semantic model automatically extracts signals from metadata that already exists in your Dataverse environment: table and column descriptions, table relationships, views, forms, and optionally sample data rows.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Enabling Sample table rows lets the model use selected row values as context.
claims.quote: When available and enabled, it uses a selection of row values to give agents context about the table's content.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Sample data rows are off by default.
claims.quote: Sample data rows are turned off by default.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The semantic model automatically regenerates every 12 hours.
claims.quote: The semantic model regenerates automatically every 12 hours to reflect schema changes.

claims.claim: An administrator can request a manual regeneration.
claims.quote: To request an earlier run after saving configuration or changing Dataverse metadata, select Regenerate.

claims.claim: Initial model generation can take up to two hours.
claims.quote: Initial generation can take up to two hours

claims.claim: Work IQ and semantic model configuration do not replace existing access permissions.
claims.quote: Making these connections available doesn't replace existing access permissions. Work IQ respects the user, agent, and application access already configured for the underlying business data.

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments subject to exceptions.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments created for new or existing tenants. The following environments are exceptions:
claims.fix: After the scoped default statement, add: 'The older Manage feature settings reference still lists Turn on Dataverse intelligence (Work IQ) for agents and AI experiences as Off by default; the Work IQ default-settings page gives the newer, environment-qualified default.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/settings-features#dataverse-intelligence-preview.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope
claims.claim: Nonproduction environments, including trial, sandbox and developer environments, are exceptions to default Work IQ enablement.
claims.quote: Nonproduction environments: This exception applies to trial, sandbox, and developer environments.

claims.claim: Microsoft deferred the previously documented November 2026 default-enablement plan for existing environments.
claims.quote: The plan to turn on Business Applications in Work IQ for existing environments that aren't listed as exceptionshas been deferred from the previously documented November 2026 schedule.

claims.claim: Sales agent has access to all columns in entities added through its administrator settings.
claims.quote: Sales agent will have access to all columns in the added entities (tables in Dynamics 365 or objects in Salesforce).

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Removing a table from the semantic model controls its inclusion in the model's context.
claims.quote: Table selection and signal settings define the context of the semantic model. They don't override or replace Dataverse security roles, table-, column-, or record-level access controls, or application-level configurations.

claims.claim: Managing the semantic model needs System Administrator or the combination of Dataverse Search, Semantic Model and Environment Maker.
claims.quote: You need either of the following security roles to manage the semantic model: System Administrator -or- Dataverse Search, Semantic Model and Environment Maker.

claims.claim: Salesforce admins must also assign a security role in the msdyn_viva environment in Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: If you are a Salesforce admin, you must assign the security role in the msdyn_viva environment in Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: Learn documents msdyn_viva as a Trial environment that can be converted to Production.
claims.quote: The msdyn_viva environment is of type Trial. If you need to convert the environment to Production, follow the steps in the Convert the sales environment from Trial to Production article.

claims.claim: The semantic-model documentation describes interpretation context, not a write capability of the model.
claims.quote: Searched: Sales agent CRM entities list semantic model data scope limit write capability. Opened semantic-model-overview, fine-tune-semantic-model-signals and set-up-sales-chat; no write capability is assigned to the semantic model itself.

claims.claim: Sales agent and Copilot in Dynamics 365 Sales share the SalesSpecificQnA semantic model.
claims.quote: Sales Agent and Copilot in Dynamics 365 Sales both use SalesSpecificQnA

claims.claim: Changes to a shared semantic model affect every associated app or agent.
claims.quote: If multiple apps or agents share the same semantic model ... changes to that model apply to all experiences associated with it.

claims.claim: Generated summaries, views and relationships are read-only.
claims.quote: Generated summaries, views, and relationships are read-only.

claims.claim: Glossary entries can supply business definitions to correct interpretations automatic extraction misses.
claims.quote: Use the glossary to add business definitions and context that automatic extraction might not capture.

claims.claim: Semantic-model glossary changes are picked up during regeneration rather than simply on saving the entry.
claims.quote: Changes are picked up during regeneration. To request an earlier run instead of waiting for the scheduled cycle, see Regenerate the semantic model. Regeneration must complete before you check the updated model.

claims.claim: The semantic model does not support environment copy or move.
claims.quote: No ALM support. The semantic model currently doesn't support environment copy or move operations.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with: 'The overview says environment copy or move is unsupported; the configuration guide separately says semantic models are solution-aware and can move configuration through solutions.' Both pages are already cited: https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/data-platform/semantic-model-overview and https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/data-platform/fine-tune-semantic-model-signals#add-semantic-model-to-a-solution.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: After an environment copy or move, restart the model by turning Work IQ, formerly Dataverse intelligence, off and back on.
claims.quote: After any environment copy or move, turn Dataverse Intelligence off and back on in the Power Platform Admin Center to force a restart.

claims.claim: Learn warns that the preview setup may have restricted functionality.
claims.quote: Preview features aren’t meant for production use and might have restricted functionality.

claims.claim: Enabling Dataverse search can increase storage usage through indexes for searchable tables.
claims.quote: Enabling Dataverse search can increase storage usage because indexes are created for searchable tables.

claims.claim: Semantic modelling uses additional storage for search indexes.
claims.quote: Some features use extra storage for search indexes. These features include semantic modeling and access to Power Apps and Dynamics 365 data through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Removing unwanted tables from Dataverse search can reduce index-related storage costs.
claims.quote: To reduce index-related storage costs, remove tables that you don't want to be indexed.

claims.claim: Dynamics 365 tables removed from Dataverse search cannot be queried in Sales agent.
claims.quote: However, if you remove tables from Dataverse search, you can't query them in Sales agent.

claims.claim: The default-settings page instead calls for an environment administrator account for the environment-level setting.

claims.claim: The tenant-level setting calls for a tenant administrator account.
